# Account Verification Standard (v4, effective 2025-03-01)

Applies to every account, internet-only or with Home Phone.

1. Before you discuss, change or disclose anything about an account, verify the caller or writer is the account
   holder or an authorized user listed on the account.
2. Accepted: the 6-digit account PIN, or a one-time passcode (OTP) sent by text or email to the contact details
   on file. Do not verify with date of birth, the last four of an SSN, the service address, or other details a
   stranger could find. (Federal CPNI rules forbid using "readily available biographical information" for Home
   Phone call detail; Northbeam applies the same rule to all accounts.)
3. Email and chat tickets that come from the email address or app login on file count as verified for questions
   about that account's own bills and payments. Any change to the account (plan, address, contacts, PIN,
   authorized users) still needs the PIN or an OTP.
4. Authorized users are listed under "Authorized users" in Beam360. A spouse or relative who is not listed is not
   authorized, whatever they say.
5. If the caller cannot verify: you may take a message, give general information that is not about the account
   (outage status for an area, plan prices), or offer an OTP to the contact on file.
6. Suspected impersonation or account takeover: do not tip off the caller; end politely, note the account, and
   send a referral to Account Security (Ray Delgado's queue) with the time, number and what was asked.
7. Changes to the PIN, email or address on file trigger an automatic notice to the contact details already on
   file.

# Outage credits (v3, effective 2025-11-01)

- Eligible: a confirmed network outage (an incident number from NOC) of 4 hours or more at the service address.
- Amount: one day of the monthly service charge (monthly charge / 30) for each started 24-hour period of the
  outage, for internet and Home Phone separately. Round to the cent.
- Do not give restoration times (ETR) that NOC has not posted on the incident page.
- Home Phone customers lose dial tone, including 911, during a fiber outage. Tell them to use a mobile phone for
  emergencies; customers with medical alarms on Home Phone get a priority callback when service returns.
- Tag every contact with the incident number.

versions.author: worker
versions.content:
# Cancellations and retention (v6)

- Customers may cancel by phone, chat, email or in the app. Process the cancellation the customer asks for; do
  not require them to call another number.
- You may present one retention offer from the Offer Library before processing. If the customer says no,
  process the cancellation.
- Final bill: service is billed a month in advance; a cancellation is prorated to the day and credited on the
  final bill. Equipment must be returned within 30 days to avoid the $150.00 unreturned-equipment fee.
- California customers: tell them they may cancel at any time by saying they want to cancel, before any
  retention offer (Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code 17602(e)). Voicemail cancellation requests are called back within
  one business day.

versions.content:
# Card data handling

- Never take card numbers, expiry dates or security codes by voice, chat or email.
- By phone: transfer the customer to Secure Pay (the IVR) from the softphone; the recording pauses automatically.
- By chat or email: send the payment link from Beam360. If a customer pastes card data into a chat or email, do
  not repeat it; use Redact in the ticket to remove it, and tell the customer you have removed it.
- You may see the last four digits of a card on file in Beam360; you may read them back to confirm which card.

versions.content:
# Payment arrangements and late fees

- Bills are issued on the 1st and due on the 18th. A $10.00 late fee posts 15 days after the due date if the
  balance is unpaid.
- Tier 1 may set up an arrangement up to $250.00, in at most two installments, the last within 30 days.
  Arrangements stop collection activity while kept.
- Service is suspended for non-payment 45 days after the due date; customers get a written notice 10 days
  before.

# Escalation paths

| Team | Takes | How | Response |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Tier 2 Billing (Lena Kowalczyk's queue) | refunds, fee reversals, credits over authority, billing errors | email t2-billing@ with account, amounts, confirmation numbers | 1 business day |
| Tier 2 Technical (Jamal Whitfield's queue) | faults outside a known incident, repeat tech issues | ticket transfer with test results | same day |
| Field Ops dispatch (Brent Olsen) | technician visits | dispatch request with access notes | next available window |
| Loyalty (Shauna Bell) | customers asking for offers outside the library, repeat cancellers | warm transfer or callback request | same day |
| Account Security (Ray Delgado) | impersonation, takeover, suspicious requests | referral form, never tell the caller | 4 hours |
| Compliance (Hannah Stiles) | regulator complaints, legal threats, recording and consent questions | email | 1 business day |

Every escalation states: account number, what the customer asked, what you already did, amounts and dates, and
what the customer was told to expect.

versions.content:
# Case notes

Every contact gets a case note in the ticket or the call record before you take the next contact:
reason for contact; verification method; what you found; what you did or promised (with amounts, dates and
reference numbers); what happens next and who owns it. No card data, no PINs, no passwords in notes. Use
plain sentences; others will read them while the customer is on the line.

# Home Phone 911 address and 911 limitations (v2, effective 2025-06-01)

Home Phone is interconnected VoIP. Federal rules (47 CFR 9.11) require us to hold a Registered Location for
every line and to tell every subscriber when 911 may not work.

- New Home Phone line: confirm the 911 address (the service address unless the customer says otherwise) before
  the line is activated, and read the 911 notice: "Home Phone and 911 calls will not work if your power or your
  internet service is out, or if the phone equipment is moved to another address without updating your 911
  address." Record the customer's yes in the case note.
- Moves: update the 911 address in Beam360 (Home Phone > 911 address) to the new address for the move date, in
  the same contact as the move order. A line moved without the update sends 911 calls to the old address.
- Customers can also update the 911 address themselves in the app (Home Phone > Emergency address).
